newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy opposition to vote for reform commission.
newsitem.headline: Italy opposition to vote for reform commission.

text.p: Italy's opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance decided on Tuesday to support a government proposal to set up a commission of both houses of parliament to draft reforms to the constitution, an alliance leader said.

"The Freedom Alliance...will give an indication...in favour of the bi-cameral commission," Pierferdinando Casini, head of the centrist CCD party, said after the bloc's leaders met to iron out differences over which way to vote on the proposal.
The Senate (upper house) is due to vote on Wednesday.

The far-right National Alliance, which had caused a rift with Freedom Alliance (AN) leader Silvio Berlusconi because it wanted a constituent assembly instead of a bi-cameral commission to draft the reforms, said it too had given its backing.

"We will vote for the bi-cameral commission," Giulio Maceratini, AN's Senate leader told reporters. He said the party was "satisfied" because the whole bloc would press for guarantees it had demanded regarding the outcome of the reforms.

Italy has tried to modernise its 1948 constitution for years but with scant progress. The lower Chamber of Deputies is due to vote on the bi-cameral commission on January 21 and if approved, the 70-member body would have until June to work out changes.
